newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam wants more ideology in education, science.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam wants more ideology in education, science.

text.p: Vietnam's Communist Party newspaper, the Nhan Dan daily, on Thursday called for greater emphasis on ideology in education and science.
A front-page editorial warned that the negative consequence of reform policies introduced in the late 1980s required a strengthening of management by Party cells.
Party cells are local political units which operate across Vietnam inside businesses, communes, schools and a host of other institutions to ensure compliance with government and party policy.

"As the local political nucleus, Party cells in the fields of education and training, science and technology should ... gather and unite intellectuals and teachers to strictly implement Party resolutions," it said.
Vietnam's communist government is sensitive to any indications that its leading role in society might be threatened.
Top officials regularly stress the need to maintain cultural and ideological correctness and earlier this year called for the establishment of party cells in foreign joint ventures.
In recent months they have also emphasised the importance of education as a means of combating declining morals and social vice.

The Nhan Dan editorial said an easing of controls by Party cells had caused "many negative things and obstacles to appear, sometimes caused losses, destroyed the production, environment and life of the people and produced signs of deviation ..."
